seo.title: Reynolds Number Calculator - Pipe Flow
seo.description: Calculate Reynolds number for fluid flow regimes — Determines laminar vs turbulent flow conditions

formula.explanation: Re = ρ × v × D / μ. Density (kg/m³), velocity (m/s), diameter (m), dynamic viscosity (Pa·s). Re < 2300 laminar, 2300-4000 transitional, >4000 turbulent.

content.introduction: Reynolds number is the dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces in a fluid. It determines whether flow is laminar (Re < 2300), transitional (2300-4000), or turbulent (Re > 4000). Essential for friction factor selection and pressure drop calculations.

example.description: Water at 2 m/s in 100mm pipe: Re = 200,000 → turbulent flow

faq.q: What is a good Reynolds number for pipe flow?
faq.a: For most industrial applications, turbulent flow with Re > 10,000 is desirable for good mixing and heat transfer. Laminar flow (Re < 2300) is common in very viscous fluids or small pipes.
Re determines which pressure drop equation to use and is required to find the friction factor in the Darcy-Weisbach equation.

faq.q: How do I convert kinematic viscosity units?
faq.a: 1 cSt = 1 mm²/s = 1×10⁻⁶ m²/s. To convert cSt to m²/s multiply by 1e-6. Dynamic viscosity μ (Pa·s) = kinematic viscosity ν (m²/s) × density ρ (kg/m³); 1 cP = 0.001 Pa·s.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Reynolds Number
sections.body:
**Viscosity units**

- 1 cSt = 1 mm²/s = 1×10⁻⁶ m²/s
- 1 cP = 0.001 Pa·s = 0.001 kg/(m·s)
- 1 Pa·s = 1000 cP

**Density units**

- 1 kg/m³ = 0.06243 lb/ft³
- 1 lb/ft³ = 16.018 kg/m³

**Length units**

- 1 inch = 25.4 mm
- 1 m = 3.28084 ft

Re = ρVD/μ requires consistent SI units: density in kg/m³, velocity in m/s, diameter in m, dynamic viscosity in Pa·s. Convert all inputs to SI before computing.
